advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Mirror the CLI's new ConfigError boundary onto the MCP surface: teach _mcp_errors._envelope_error (or error_code_for) to classify rebar.config.ConfigError so MCP claim_ticket/transition emit a structured error_envelope instead of a raw exception.
evidence: Diff adds to CLI surface: `except ConfigError as e:` / `sys.stderr.write(f"Error: {e}\n")` / `return 1` in src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py
gates.py now raises: `raise ConfigError(f"cannot resolve {gate_label} for {ticket_id}: ...") from exc`
src/rebar/_config_coercion.py:20: `class ConfigError(ValueError):` — ConfigError derives from ValueError, not RebarError
src/rebar/_errors.py:19: `class RebarError(RuntimeError):` — RebarError is a RuntimeError, so ConfigError is not an instance of it

src/rebar/_mcp_errors.py:56: `if isinstance(exc, (RebarError, CommandError, mismatch_type, llm_error_type)):` — ConfigError matches none of these, so _envelope_error returns None (line 61) and the raw exception re-raises through the MCP tool guard (src/rebar/_mcp_errors.py:104-106)
src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:289: `rebar.claim(ticket_id, assignee=assignee, force=force)` — the MCP claim adapter routes through the now-raising gate path
advisory.finding: The new caller-reachable ConfigError-on-unreadable-config failure is given a clean operator-facing boundary on the CLI adapter (_cli/__init__.py adds `except ConfigError -> 'Error: ...' + exit 1`), but the sibling MCP write adapter was not updated to mirror it: rebar.config.ConfigError is a ValueError, not a RebarError, so _mcp_errors._envelope_error (which only matches RebarError/CommandError/ConcurrencyMismatch/LLMError) returns None and the raw ConfigError escapes MCP claim_ticket/transition without a structured error_envelope.
scenarios: An MCP-driven agent calls claim_ticket or transition against a repo whose rebar.toml is present but unparseable: the CLI gives `Error: cannot resolve ... (operator ruling 39f8-ae7c)` + exit 1, while the MCP surface surfaces a raw/unenveloped ConfigError with no machine-readable error code for the agent to branch on.
advisory.suggested_fix: In src/rebar/_mcp_errors.py add ConfigError to the recognized set in _envelope_error (e.g. `from rebar.config import ConfigError` and include it in the isinstance tuple), and register a corresponding code (e.g. `config_unreadable`) in KNOWN_ERROR_CODES + error_code_for in src/rebar/_errors.py, so the MCP adapter renders the same failure the CLI now renders.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the fail-open -> ConfigError change on public rebar.transition/rebar.claim (unreadable config now raises) is an intended, documented, unversioned behavior change and that external consumers are accounted for.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:113-120 `except ConfigError as exc: raise ConfigError(...) from exc` replaces the prior `return GateState.UNREADABLE` fail-open skip
rebar.transition is a public export: src/rebar/__init__.py:245 `"transition",`

Consumer path: rebar.transition -> transition_close close gate -> gates.gate_enabled (gates.py:196) and rebar.claim -> _plan_review_gate_applies -> gate_enabled (gates.py:282), all of which previously proceeded on an unreadable config and now raise
This is an intentional, documented change (docs/config.md, docs/plan-review-gate.md updated; operator ruling 39f8-ae7c) but it is an unversioned behavior change on a public API surface
blocking.finding: Public library functions rebar.transition / rebar.claim change their fault-path contract: an unreadable/malformed rebar.toml that previously fail-OPENed the opt-in verify.* gate (operation PROCEEDED) now propagates a ConfigError, so external callers relying on the old fail-open behavior see a new raised exception rather than a completed operation.
scenarios: A downstream/embedding caller of rebar.transition or rebar.claim runs against a repo whose rebar.toml is temporarily malformed; the call now raises ConfigError instead of quietly completing.
